edge_sample.source_text: definition Face of a cone: A \emph{face} of a pointed cone \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is the intersection of \( \sigma \) with some hyperplane \( u^{\perp} \) for \( u \in \sigma^{\vee} \). We write \( \tau \preceq \sigma \) if \( \tau \) is a face of \( \sigma \) and
edge_sample.target_text: lemma Intersection of faces: If \( \sigma \) is a pointed cone, then the intersection of two faces of \( \sigma \) is a again face of \( \sigma \).

edge_sample.source_text: definition : A {\bf pointed cone} \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is a \( \Bbbk_{\geq 0} \)-submodule of \( N \).
edge_sample.target_text: definition : For a set \( S \subseteq N \), the {\bf cone generated by \( S \)} is the pointed cone \[ \mathrm{Cone}(S) := \mathrm{Span}_{\Bbbk_{\geq 0}}(S) \subseteq N. \]

edge_sample.target_text: lemma Face order is a lattice: Given a polyhedral cone, the partial order on its faces is a lattice. We call it the \emph{face lattice} of the cone.

edge_sample.source_text: proposition Double dual: If \( \sigma \subseteq N \) is polyhedral, then \( \sigma^{\vee\vee} = \sigma \).
edge_sample.target_text: proof : The cone \( \sigma := \mathrm{Cone}(S) \) is finitely generated, hence polyhedral by~\ref{polyhedral-of-fg}. Furthermore, we have \( \sigma^{\vee\vee} = S^{\vee\vee} \). Now apply~\ref{double-dual-polyhedral-cone}.
